description: Local-first desktop app for dictation, meeting notes, audio files, and narrated walkthroughs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Runs Parakeet, Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, or cloud APIs, with AI cleanup, LAN/Tailscale engine sharing, and MCP.

latest_release.name: OpenWhisper 2.9.0
latest_release.body:
### Added

- **Fourier 2B in Downloads.** Oruk's English fine-tune of Qwen3-ASR 1.7B is an optional **Qwen3-ASR** download on Windows x64 and Linux x86-64: the publisher's pinned 8-bit GGUF (2.19 GB), checked by size and SHA-256, with its model card for the attribution and CC BY-NC 4.0 notice. It is for noncommercial use: Downloads, Host Mode download prompts, and batch download prompts say so, and that commercial use needs a separate license from Oruk.

### Changed

- **Consistent secondary buttons and transparent wrappers in Settings and dialogs.** Meeting remote controls, context folder buttons, remote model/runtime actions, auto-paste setup, MCP retry, and collapsible card/dialog containers now match the Settings chrome without stray background seams or empty status gaps.

### Fixed

- **OpenWhisper no longer freezes after about a day on Linux/X11.** The five-minute refresh of the global shortcut hook left X server connections and threads behind, until the server refused new ones and the next refresh froze the app. A replaced hook now ends at once, even while nobody types. If the X server has no room for a new one, shortcuts keep working in the focused window and a later refresh restores the global ones. Dismissing a shortcut field without pressing a key no longer leaves its listener running. ([#141](https://github.com/Knuckles92/OpenWhisper/issues/141))
- **Cleanup reversals and snippet placeholders are validated more reliably.** Anchored cleanup reversals and validated snippet placeholder ordering.

detail.readme:
# OpenWhisper A desktop app for dictation, audio-file transcription, and meeting notes on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Transcribe with local speech models, a speech server you run, or a cloud API, then optionally use AI, including models you run yourself, to clean up the text. [Website](https://openwhisper.fiorilabs.tech/) · [Download](https://github.com/Knuckles92/OpenWhisper/releases/latest) · [Run from source](#run-from-source) · [Install](#install) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) Use a [packaged release](#install) with bundled Python and dependencies, or [run from source](#run-from-source) with uv. **Feedback:** If you’re unhappy with any part of the app, please [open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/Knuckles92/OpenWhisper/issues) and I’ll do my best to make it right ASAP.

## What it does - **Dictation:** Record from any app with a global hotkey, see a live preview on supported engines, and paste the result into the active window. - **Walkthroughs:** Talk through a task while keeping screenshots, then get a PDF, Word and Markdown document with each screenshot after the words that describe it, ready to paste into a coding agent. Review and correct saved walkthroughs, or have your own agent write one up. Windows, macOS, and Linux (X11, Hyprland); see the [Walkthrough guide](docs/walkthrough.md). - **Audio files:** Transcribe one file or a queue, keep results separate or combine them, and copy the output when ready. - **Meetings:** Capture microphone and system audio, follow a live dashboard, review searchable transcripts and AI insights, play recordings, and export. Available on Windows and macOS 13+; Linux system audio is a [preview](docs/linux-system-audio.md). - **AI cleanup:** Choose Light, Medium, or High cleanup, which handles spoken corrections and lists, then apply spelling and style rules or reusable [cleanup profiles](docs/cleanup-profiles.md), with separate text-model choices for dictation and meetings. - **Personalize:** A [dictionary](docs/personalize.md#dictionary) that steers recognition and learns from your corrections, spoken [snippets](docs/personalize.md#snippets), a tone for each kind of app, and [Command Mode](docs/personalize.md#command-mode-and-transforms) to rewrite selected text by voice or with saved transforms. - **Extras:** Hands-free recording by double-tapping the record key, mouse side buttons as shortcuts, ranked microphones with automatic fallback, an overlay language switcher, a floating Scratchpad, and Stats for dictation, meetings, files and the rest. - **Settings:** Opens on **Home**, with where your words go, the everyday controls, and what's downloaded. Everything else is in six sidebar sections (Dictation, Personalize, Automate, Meeting Mode, Models & storage, App), and the header search (Ctrl+K) finds any setting. New installs get an optional guided setup, which **File → Guided setup…** reopens. - **History:** Search, play back, retranscribe, and export transcripts as Markdown, plain text, or JSON, and switch an entry between its original and AI-cleaned versions. See [export format support](docs/export-support.md) for what each format includes. - **Agent history API (preview):** Search saved transcripts and meeting notes through an opt-in, authenticated local API. See [API setup](docs/agent-api.md). - **MCP:** Enable **Settings → Automate → API & MCP** to connect an agent to history, transcripts, and meeting insights. Optionally allow retitling and choose which settings agents may change. See [MCP setup](docs/mcp.md). - **Actions and automation:** Send what you say to a new Claude or ChatGPT chat, your coding agent, a running Claude Code session, a webhook or a program, with a shortcut or by naming it ("Claude, …"). Follow live events, run actions and change dictated text from your own tools over a local API, webhooks and MCP. See [Actions, live events and hooks](docs/automation.md). The app also includes microphone selection, a system tray where available, and dark, light, or system-matched themes. ## Install Download the package for your platform from [Releases](https://github.com/Knuckles92/OpenWhisper/releases/latest). Native packages include Python, the app dependencies, and (on Windows x64 and Linux x86_64) the `transcribe.cpp` speech runtime. Choose the **All-in-One** (`OpenWhisper-AllInOne-*`) installer on Windows or Linux to also bundle the compact English **Parakeet TDT-CTC 110M** model (~135 MB) so offline dictation, live preview, and meetings work right out of the box with no extra download. See the [code signing policy](#code-signing-policy) for how releases are built and signed. | Platform | Install | | --- | --- | | Windows | Run `OpenWhisper-Setup-.exe` (slim; downloads your speech model on first use) or `OpenWhisper-AllInOne-Setup-.exe` (ready offline out of the box). Both install per-user without admin rights and upgrade in place. | | macOS | Open the `.dmg` and drag OpenWhisper into Applications. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14+. Unless a release says it is notarized, approve first launch in **Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. Intel Macs run [from source](#run-from-source). | | Linux | Install the `.deb` on Debian 12+ / Ubuntu 22.04+, or `.pkg.tar.zst` on Arch-compatible distributions (`OpenWhisper-*` slim or `OpenWhisper-AllInOne-*` with the bundled English model). Both packages require x86_64. | On Linux, use the matching command, replacing `` with your download's version: ```bash sudo apt install "./OpenWhisper--linux-amd64.deb" # or sudo pacman -U "./OpenWhisper--linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst" ``` Launch from your app menu; Linux packages also provide `ow` and `openwhisper` commands. Opening the app again on Linux brings the existing window forward. Downloads include `SHA256SUMS.txt` for verification. Compare your file's hash using `Get-FileHash` in PowerShell, `shasum -a 256` on macOS, or `sha256sum` on Linux. Unless a release says its Windows build is signed (its `BUILD-METADATA.json` then has `"windows_signed": true`), the installer is unsigned; if SmartScreen blocks it, verify the download before choosing **More info → Run anyway**. ### macOS permissions In **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, allow **Microphone** for recording, **Screen & System Audio Recording** for meeting audio and walkthrough screenshots, and **Accessibility** for auto-paste. You can copy transcripts without Accessibility. **Settings → Home → Set up auto-paste…** shows which app to allow and checks access automatically. If an old entry is enabled but access is still missing, choose **Repair old Accessibility entry…**, then enable the current app in macOS Settings. See [macOS auto-paste setup and recovery](docs/macos-accessibility.md). When macOS asks whether OpenWhisper may use your **login** Keychain (to read saved API keys, the MCP token, or a remote engine's connection key), enter your Mac password and choose **Always Allow**. **Allow** works for that one read only, so macOS asks again at every launch. Builds that aren't notarized may ask once more after an update. ## Run from source Use **Git** and **uv** for the default source setup on Windows, Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, and Linux. On Intel Macs and older macOS versions, follow [setup with pip](CONTRIBUTING.md#setup-with-pip) so pip can select compatible dependency versions. ### One-time setup [Install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), then open a new terminal and run these commands: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Knuckles92/OpenWhisper cd OpenWhisper uv sync --locked ``` uv uses Python 3.12, downloads it if needed, and installs the versions in `uv.lock` into `.venv/`. You can run the app without activating the environment. See [development with uv](CONTRIBUTING.md#development-with-uv) for tests and editor setup. On Linux, some dependencies may require a C compiler and development headers. The launcher checks audio and Qt system libraries and prints the package-manager command for any missing dependencies. Meeting capture also needs [PulseAudio or PipeWire-Pulse](docs/linux-system-audio.md). ### Launch the app Run these commands from your `OpenWhisper` checkout folder: **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell uv run --locked python main.py ``` **macOS / Linux:** ```bash ./scripts/openwhisper ``` The macOS/Linux launcher uses `.venv/` and handles macOS app-bundle identification when Python provides a framework bundle. For macOS auto-paste, see [the framework Python setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#development-with-uv). Then follow [Get started](#get-started). ### Optional: launch from any terminal To register `ow` and `openwhisper`, run `.\install.cmd` in PowerShell on Windows or `./install.sh` on macOS/Linux once from your checkout folder. Open a new terminal, then use `ow` or `openwhisper` from any folder without activating the virtual environment. See [source launchers](CONTRIBUTING.md#source-launchers) for details. ## GPU acceleration For Local Whisper on Windows or Linux x86_64, install **GPU Acceleration** from **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines → Components**, or choose **Use this GPU** when prompted. Requires an NVIDIA driver providing CUDA 12 (525+); the CUDA Toolkit is not needed. macOS uses CPU. Source installs can also use `uv sync --locked --extra gpu` to install CUDA wheels on Windows or Linux x86_64. On Windows, launch with `uv run --locked --extra gpu python main.py`. On Linux, use `./scripts/openwhisper`. **Auto** selects a compatible compute type. **Models & engines** shows GPU memory estimates. On Windows x64 and Linux x86_64, Parakeet Unified and Qwen3-ASR share the bundled transcribe.cpp runtime, which uses Vulkan for GPU acceleration. Other speech runtimes are available in Models & engines. On Apple Silicon Macs, **Auto** runs Parakeet MLX on the Apple GPU through MLX, Parakeet and Nemotron through the **NVIDIA Speech GPU (Metal)** runtime, and Qwen3-ASR through PyTorch MPS. The Pi and OpenCode SDK meeting agents are also separate components, available on Windows, Linux and macOS. ## Updates OpenWhisper asks GitHub for the latest release when it starts and every 4 hours while it runs, sending only the app version. A newer release shows as an **Update to x.y.z** button in the title bar and the tray menu until you update. To check yourself, use **OpenWhisper → Check for Updates** on macOS or **Help → Check for Updates** on Windows and Linux. Turn automatic checks off in **Settings → App → General → Updates**. Git checkouts don't check on their own. To try releases a few days early, turn on **Get beta updates** in the same group: OpenWhisper then also offers GitHub prereleases, whichever of the newest beta and the newest regular release has the higher version. Betas are verified exactly like regular releases. Turning it off never downgrades: you keep the beta you have and get the next regular release that is newer (often the same build, once it is promoted). While GitHub's API is rate-limited, beta copies are offered only regular releases until it answers again. - **Windows:** Apply the in-app update or follow the setup prompt. - **macOS:** The verified update installs and restarts the app, restoring the previous version if startup fails. If the app cannot replace itself, it opens the verified DMG for replacement in Applications. - **Linux:** Install the new package with the same command used for installation. - **From source:** Run `git pull --ff-only` and `uv sync --locked`. Include `--extra gpu` if you installed CUDA wheels with uv. When a package upgrade or pull replaces the app while it runs, OpenWhisper offers **Restart now** once nothing is recording or transcribing. ## Get started 1. Open **Settings → Dictation → Voice model** and choose a speech backend. New Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 installs default to **Parakeet Unified** (English, with its `transcribe.cpp` CPU/Vulkan runtime bundled in the installer), and Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 14 or later default to **Parakeet MLX**; other platforms default to Local Whisper. Dictating in another language? Switch to **Parakeet TDT v3**, **Local Whisper**, or **Qwen3-ASR** from Guided Setup or **Voice model → Languages I dictate in**. Existing installs keep the engine they use. 2. Download the model (and any optional runtime for other engines) through Guided Setup or **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines**, or add an OpenAI key in **Settings → App → API keys** for cloud transcription. 3. Choose your microphone in **Settings → Dictation → Recording**. On macOS, grant the [required permissions](#macos-permissions). 4. Use **Quick Record** or the recording hotkey. Stop recording to transcribe. Dictation follows your clipboard and auto-paste settings. If the remote engine goes offline before transcription, the recording overlay shows up to three reconnect attempts within 12 seconds. If transcription fails, open **History** to play the saved recording or choose **Retry transcription**. Recovered transcripts and **Upload File** results are ready to copy in the app. For meetings, open **Meeting Mode**. Add an optional brief to guide AI notes and the live copilot; you can edit it during the meeting. After transcription, **Continue in the background** lets you start another meeting while reports finish. Find results in **Past Meetings**. Before the first meeting, setup checks for missing speech runtimes and models and offers to download them. Choose **Check microphone and system audio**, then speak and play sound through the output your calls use. Test audio is discarded. You can start after the check even if setup is incomplete, but missing models or audio may prevent a usable transcript. On macOS, denied system-audio permission offers a microphone-only start. Reopen these checks with **Meeting setup…**; Linux preview hosts include the same setup. Unless you save a meeting-specific model, compatible computers reuse your selected native Parakeet model. Optional [insight review](docs/meeting-insight-review.md) helps clarify uncertain decisions and commitments. [Fast judgments](docs/typesafe-fast-judgments.md) add citation checks, meaning-based history search, and live meeting cues; enable them under **Meeting Mode → Fast judgments**, with a TypeSafe key, the OpenRouter key you already use, or your own text model. With a model on this computer they send nothing, and live cues and history search work even with AI insights off. ### Hotkeys Change shortcuts and choose **Toggle** or **Push and hold** in **Settings → App → Hotkeys**. Toggle starts and stops recording with successive presses; push-and-hold records until you release the shortcut. | Action | Windows / Linux | macOS | | --- | --- | --- | | Start/stop recording | Numpad `*` | `Control+Option+R` | | Cancel | Numpad `-` | `Control+Option+Escape` | | Enable/disable program | `Ctrl+Alt+Numpad *` | `Control+Option+Shift+R` | | Minimize to tray | `Ctrl+Alt+M` | `Control+Option+M` | | Paste latest walkthrough | `Ctrl+Shift+F12` | `Control+Shift+F12` | In push-and-hold mode, double-tap the record shortcut to keep recording hands-free, then press it again to stop. Command Mode, the Scratchpad, switching dictation language, and pasting the original of your last dictation have optional shortcuts with no default. On Windows and X11, mouse side buttons (Mouse 4 and Mouse 5) can be shortcuts too. On X11 Linux, hotkeys also reach the focused app. Omarchy supports desktop shortcuts and auto-paste; other native Wayland desktops use focused-window shortcuts and manual paste. macOS auto-paste requires Accessibility permission; global hotkeys do not. ### Omarchy / Hyprland OpenWhisper adapts to Omarchy 3 and 4 with a compact interface and desktop colors. Hyprland manages window placement and sizing; Omarchy mode supports desktop shortcuts and auto-paste on Hyprland 0.55+. Choose **Settings → App → Appearance → Theme → Omarchy desktop** to follow your desktop palette. An optional [Omarchy 4 bar widget](integrations/omarchy) provides recording controls, status, and live text. ## Speech models | Backend | Models | Platform / device | Workflows | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Local Whisper | Standard Whisper sizes, turbo, Distil-Whisper | All platforms, CPU; NVIDIA CUDA on Windows/Linux | Dictation with preview, uploads, meetings | | Parakeet | TDT 0.6B v3; Orukeet TDT 0.6B community adaptation | Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 CPU / NVIDIA GPU; Apple Silicon CPU / Apple GPU (Metal); Intel Mac CPU | Dictation with preview, uploads, meeting chunks | | Parakeet MLX | TDT 0.6B v3, MLX Community weights | Apple Silicon, macOS 14+: Apple GPU through Metal or CPU | Dictation with preview, uploads, meeting chunks | | Parakeet Unified | Unified EN 0.6B (native preview); TDT-CTC 110M (compact, included in All-in-One installers), English | Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 CPU / GPU through Vulkan (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) | Dictation with preview, uploads; meetings (TDT-CTC 110M) | | Qwen3-ASR | 0.6B, 1.7B; Fourier 2B (English, noncommercial, Windows/Linux) | Windows x64 / Linux x86_64 CPU or Vulkan GPU; Apple Silicon CPU or Apple GPU (MPS) for 0.6B / 1.7B | Dictation, uploads | | Nemotron Streaming | 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B | Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 CPU / NVIDIA GPU; Apple Silicon CPU / Apple GPU (Metal); Intel Mac CPU | Dictation with preview, uploads, meetings with native preview | | Moonshine | Streaming Small / Medium, English | Windows x64 CPU; Apple Silicon CPU, macOS 15+ | Dictation, uploads, meetings with native preview | | API | OpenAI: GPT-Transcribe; GPT-4o Transcribe, GPT-4o Mini Transcribe, and Whisper until OpenAI retires them on February 26, 2027. Groq: Whisper Large v3 / Turbo. Your own server: whatever it serves | OpenAI or Groq in the cloud (API key required), or an OpenAI-compatible speech server you run: Speaches, LocalAI, vLLM, whisper.cpp, or custom | Dictation, uploads | | Remote computer | Whichever engine the paired computer has selected | Another computer running OpenWhisper on your network | Dictation with that engine's preview, uploads, meetings with a supported host model | - **Models & engines:** Install both the model and its required runtime in **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines**. Each entry shows its size, publisher, license, and download checks. - **Languages:** Choose a supported language or **Auto** for detection. Coverage varies by engine; Moonshine and Parakeet Unified are English-only. Language selection controls transcription, not translation. - **Apple Silicon:** Choose **Auto** to use the Apple GPU where supported. See [GPU acceleration](#gpu-acceleration) for engine-specific support. See [speech model details](docs/speech-models.md) for language coverage, platform requirements, download verification, and Orukeet and Fourier 2B's license and validation status. ### Custom Whisper models Choose **Add custom models…** in **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines**, **Dictation → Voice model**, or **Meeting Mode → Voice & speakers**. - **Local files:** Choose a model folder or a parent folder containing several models. OpenWhisper lists complete model folders for you to select. - **Hugging Face:** Enter an `owner/model` repository and, optionally, a subfolder such as `ct2_int8_float16`. **Find on Hugging Face** lists compatible model folders without downloading weights. You can also discover models already in the local Hugging Face cache. Click **Add selected**, then choose a model in **Voice model** or **Voice & speakers** to load it. - **Format:** CTranslate2 Whisper folders with `model.bin`, a valid `config.json`, and `tokenizer.json`. Convert original PyTorch weights before use. - **Storage:** Downloads follow your Hugging Face policy; cached models load offline. Removing a custom entry keeps its source files. ### Custom models for other engines Choose **Add custom… → Local speech model (GGUF / ORT / Safetensors)…** in **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines** to use your own model file with Parakeet, Nemotron Streaming, Parakeet Unified, Qwen3-ASR, Moonshine or Parakeet MLX. **Runtime format** lists the formats with a runtime on this computer. Then choose the model for that engine in **Voice model** or **Voice & speakers**. - **Format:** the same kind of file the engine's own models use. Parakeet, Nemotron and Parakeet Unified load a `.gguf` file, as does Qwen3-ASR on Windows and Linux. Qwen3-ASR on a Mac loads a Safetensors model folder, Moonshine a folder of `.ort` files (choose Small or Medium), and Parakeet MLX a folder with `config.json` and Safetensors weights. OpenWhisper checks the format when you add it. A model the engine can't run fails when it loads, with the engine's message. - **Storage:** the model is used from where it is, without copying, and nothing is downloaded. Removing it keeps its files. If you move the file, add it again. - **Paired computers:** a host never offers its custom models to paired computers, and a paired computer can't switch the host to one. ### Remote engine Use another computer's OpenWhisper engine for dictation, uploads, or meetings: 1. On the computer with the engine, open **Settings → Dictation → Remote engine**, choose **Share this computer**, and turn on **Share this computer's engine**. Allow OpenWhisper through the firewall if Windows asks. 2. On the other computer, open the same page, choose **Use another computer**, find the host on your network or tailnet, and click **Connect**. Compare the six-digit number on both screens, then click **Allow** on the host only if they match. If the host isn't listed, use **Enter an address** on the client and **Show a pairing code** on the host. 3. Click **Use for dictation**, or choose **Remote computer** as the recording engine. **View → Host Mode** turns a computer that mostly serves others into a host dashboard: sharing status and address, the engine served, who's connected and what they asked for. The host's selected engine handles transcription. Traffic is encrypted and limited to paired computers; remove access under **Paired computers**. While the host is loading its speech engine, it tells paired clients to retry audio requests that have yet to start. Quick Record keeps the recording on the client through a brief restart and makes it available in History if the connection stays down. Remote Quick Record reserves the host from the start of capture through saving, even with live preview off. On Omarchy, an unattended updater can [reserve the idle host for a restart](docs/host-updates.md) without using a fixed maintenance window. If macOS Keychain refuses to save the connection key, click **Retry Keychain access** and choose **Allow** or **Always Allow** when macOS asks. If no prompt appears, use **Open Keychain Access**, unlock the **login** keychain and check the **OpenWhisper** item's **Access Control**, then retry. The approved connection stays in memory while OpenWhisper is running, so retrying does not need another pairing code or approval from the host. The connection key is only saved in the OS credential store. - **Meetings:** Select **Remote computer** in **Settings → Meeting Mode → Voice & speakers → Speech engine**. Audio goes to the host for transcription; capture, recordings, and transcripts stay on the computer running the meeting. - **Host models:** Use **Manage host models** (or switch to the paired host in **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines**) to choose or download a model and install speech runtimes. The host must first enable **Allow paired computers to manage models**. - **Shared history:** Enable **Allow the paired host to query this computer's history** on the client so agents on the host can search it while the client is online. See [MCP setup](docs/mcp.md#query-paired-clients-directly) for queries and offline copies. - **Away from home:** Install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download) on both computers. Hosts on your tailnet appear in the app; computers on the same Tailscale account can connect without a pairing code when the host allows it. ## AI cleanup and meeting intelligence Use AI cleanup to polish dictation and meeting intelligence to generate notes and insights. Each has its own text-model settings. - **Dictation:** Enable **Settings → Dictation → AI cleanup**, choose a cleanup level, and choose who runs it: an installed Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode with its own sign-in, or a text model below. The **Thinking level** lists only the levels the chosen model accepts. Add words to the **Dictionary**, pick a tone per kind of app in **Styles**, teach other behaviour in **Learned rules**, or use [Profiles](docs/cleanup-profiles.md) for reusable formats. See [Personalize dictation](docs/personalize.md). - **Providers:** OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI, Groq, OpenCode Go/Zen, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Add keys in **Settings → App → API keys**; the local servers are preconfigured with their standard local addresses and need no key — just run the server. **Edit** changes its address or sets an optional API key variable. The picker marks local servers that are running, reads each model's context and thinking support from the server, and lists only models that generate text. - **OpenAI cleanup:** The suggested model is `gpt-6-luna`. Saved OpenAI cleanup assignments using the old `gpt-4o-mini` default resolve to Luna; other models, providers, and saved meeting assignments are kept. Thinking **Off** explicitly requests `reasoning.effort: none` through the Responses API. Cleanup remains off by default, and fresh text-model assignments still use OpenRouter Free. The first time cleanup is on with no model chosen, a signed-in Claude Code or Codex found on this computer is offered instead, once; it is used only if you say yes. - **Meetings:** Choose an engine in **Settings → Meeting Mode → Intelligence** using the options below. | Meeting engine | Setup | | --- | --- | | Pi (default) | Uses your selected text endpoint and API key. Install from **Models & storage → Models & engines → Components** where available. | | Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode | Select an installed agent's tile to use its sign-in, providers, and models. Install, update, and sign in to the agent yourself. | | OpenCode SDK | Install from **Models & storage → Models & engines → Components** where available, then select it under **Agent core**. | Meeting passes count toward the installed agent's account or API usage. These agents refresh live insights less often. If an engine is unavailable, select another or continue recording without AI insights. See [AI and meeting setup](docs/meeting-intelligence.md) for custom endpoints, environment variables, agent behavior, and compatibility with older settings. ## Offline use Downloaded speech models load from the local cache without network metadata checks. Install any required runtime before going offline. Choose whether to ask, allow, or block missing-model downloads in **Settings → Models & storage → Models & engines → When a model is missing from this computer**. Set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` before launch to block model downloads entirely. Cloud transcription and remote text providers still need a network connection; speech and text servers on this computer do not. See [Network and privacy](docs/network-and-privacy.md) for every connection the app can make. Only the update check (at launch and every 4 hours) is on by default, and there is no telemetry.
More screenshots

## Code signing policy Windows installers are not signed yet. We are applying for free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/). - **Builds:** Every release is built from this repository's source by the [Build installers](.github/workflows/build-installers.yml) GitHub Actions workflow. Only those builds are signed. - **Committers and reviewers:** [Knuckles92](https://github.com/Knuckles92). Changes from other contributors arrive as pull requests and are reviewed before merging. - **Approvers:** [Knuckles92](https://github.com/Knuckles92) approves each release for signing. - **Privacy policy:** OpenWhisper has no telemetry. The only connection it makes without being asked is the update check, which you can turn off. [Network and privacy](docs/network-and-privacy.md) lists every connection the app can make. ## Contributing and license See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup, validation, pull requests, and adding a provider or engine. Release history lives in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Participation follows the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). OpenWhisper builds on OpenAI Whisper, faster-whisper, NVIDIA NeMo-Speech.cpp, Qwen3-ASR, and Moonshine, with converted Whisper weights from Systran and Mobius Labs. The app source is [MIT licensed](LICENSE); model weights and dependencies retain their own licenses. See [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
